title: [CQ-C02] Bounded repository source provider
description:
Objective: Retrieve source/patterns/callers/config/tests from immutable manifests with bounded time, bytes and concurrency.

Deliverable: Bounded repository source provider. This is task C02 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): C01, R09.

implementationPlan.description:
Shared bounded raw Git read in the existing read-only trust envelope (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/cachedPlanPaths.ts). Behavior-preserving for every current caller: submit_plan's findCachedPlanPaths and delivery/requiredChecks.ts keep calling `git(label, args, opts)` exactly as today.
(a) Move the hardened invocation that runGit builds inline into private helpers (e.g. readOnlyGitArgs(cwd, args) / readOnlyGitEnv()) and make runGit use them with byte-identical argv/env: strip every GIT_* variable; GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=NUL on win32 else /dev/null; GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; `--no-optional-locks --no-replace-objects -c protocol.allow=never -c safe.directory=<cwd>`; windowsHide; no shell. The `config` exit-1 special case stays in runGit only.
(b) Export `interface GitHeadResult { stdout: Buffer; truncated: boolean; exitCode: number | null; stderr: string }`, `type GitHeadRunner = (args: string[], cwd: string, timeout: number, maxBytes: number) => Promise<GitHeadResult>` and `runGitHead`, built on the same promisified execFile and helpers plus `encoding: 'buffer'` and `maxBuffer: maxBytes`. maxBytes must be a positive safe integer (else throw before spawning). Exit 0 -> { stdout, truncated: false, exitCode: 0, stderr: '' }. stdout overflow (error.code === 'ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER' with a Buffer error.stdout; verified on Node 24: Node kills the child and keeps exactly the first maxBuffer bytes) -> { stdout: error.stdout.subarray(0, maxBytes), truncated: true, exitCode: null }. An ordinary non-zero exit (numeric error.code, error.killed falsy) resolves { stdout, truncated: false, exitCode: code, stderr: first stderr line, max 240 chars } so the caller interprets codes such as git grep's 1 = no match. Spawn errors (ENOENT), timeouts and signals are rethrown unchanged.
(c) openProjectGit gains an optional 4th parameter `head: GitHeadRunner = runGitHead` and returns the existing `git` closure with one added method (Object.assign): `head(label, args, maxBytes)` runs head(args, root, remaining, maxBytes) on the SAME canonical root and SAME shared deadline, with the same 'budget exhausted before the step started' guard and the same failure(`git ${label}`, error) wrapping. Trust checks, BUDGET_MS, MAX_BUFFER, describeFailure and findCachedPlanPaths stay unchanged.
Tests, appended to src/util/cachedPlanPaths.test.ts (its hoisted vi.mock of node:child_process execFile is exactly what these unit tests need; never put real-git tests there): (1) exit 0 returns a Buffer, truncated false, exitCode 0; (2) overflow returns exactly the first maxBytes bytes with truncated true; (3) exit 1 resolves exitCode 1 with the first stderr line; (4) a killed/timeout error and an ENOENT error reject; (5) runGitHead sends the same hardened argv/env as runGit (safe.directory=<cwd> exactly once, a stubbed GIT_DIR removed, NOSYSTEM/GLOBAL/NO_LAZY_FETCH/TERMINAL_PROMPT set, windowsHide true, encoding 'buffer', maxBuffer = maxBytes); (6) maxBytes 0, -1 and 1.5 reject before execFile is called; (7) openProjectGit(...).head uses cwd = realpath(root) and a timeout no larger than the remaining shared budget, and after the deadline throws 'git <label>: budget exhausted before the step started' without calling the head runner (mock performance.now like the existing deadline test). Every existing test in the file stays byte-unchanged and green. Error handling: no new catch swallows an error it does not name; overflow and ordinary non-zero exit are the only non-throwing outcomes.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.ts, the new home for CQ-C context providers (import StateManager as a TYPE only; no runtime import of src/state), with the request/result contract and pure validation. It is a library: do NOT register an MCP tool and do NOT wire it into get_context. Activation, the packet (C01) and docs are later tasks.
Contract (export all):
- type SourcePurpose = 'source' | 'pattern' | 'caller' | 'config' | 'test'.
- type SourceQuery = { id: string; purpose: SourcePurpose; op: 'read'; path: string } | { id: string; purpose: SourcePurpose; op: 'search'; literal: string; paths?: string[] }.
- type SourceItemStatus = 'served' | 'truncated' | 'omitted' | 'missing' | 'refused' | 'unavailable'.
- interface SourceMatch { path: string; line: number; text: string }.
- interface SourceItem { id; purpose; op; status; reason?: string (present for every status except served); path?; oid?; mode?; size?; content?: string; matches?: SourceMatch[]; bytes: number }. bytes = UTF-8 bytes served (content for a read; sum of path + text over search matches).
- interface RepositorySource { manifest: { commit: string }; items: SourceItem[] (exactly one per query, in query order, ids preserved); complete: boolean (true iff every item is served); limitations: string[] (sorted unique codes); bytes: number (sum of item bytes) }.
- SOURCE_LIMITS defaults: timeBudgetMs 3000 (may be raised to at most 10000), maxQueries 32, maxFileBytes 65536, maxSearchBytes 65536, maxMatches 200, maxTotalBytes 262144, maxLiteralChars 200, maxScopePaths 16, maxPathspecChars 24000. options.limits may lower any limit; a non-positive, non-integer or above-ceiling value is INVALID_INPUT, never clamped.
- The manifest is a full lowercase 40- or 64-hex Git COMMIT id: immutable and content-addressed. Never a ref name, HEAD, the working tree or an uncommitted overlay.
Export validateSourceRequest(commit, queries, limits). It throws invalidInput(field, reason) (code MoeErrorCode.INVALID_INPUT, codeName 'INVALID_INPUT') before any process, lock or filesystem access for: commit not /^(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$/; queries not an array, empty, or longer than maxQueries; a query that is not a plain object; unknown op or purpose; id not a non-empty string of at most 128 chars, or duplicated; a read path or search scope that is not exactly its own normalizeAffectedFile() form (refuses '../x', 'a/../b', '/etc/passwd', 'C:/x', a backslash path like 'a\b', './a', 'a//b', leading/trailing spaces) or contains NUL, U+FFFD, C0/C1 controls, U+2028 or U+2029 (same rule as the private normalizedPath in delivery/requiredChecks.ts; mirror it, do not export it); a literal that is empty, longer than maxLiteralChars, or contains NUL, CR or LF (git -F treats newlines as several patterns); more than maxScopePaths scopes; and a sum of (length + 3) over every distinct pathspec the lookup will pass (each path and scope plus all of its ancestor prefixes) above maxPathspecChars, which keeps the one bounded ls-tree under the Windows command-line limit.
Tests: new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.test.ts. This file must NOT vi.mock node:child_process, because step 4 adds real-git fixtures to it. One it.each row per refusal listed above, each asserting { code: MoeErrorCode.INVALID_INPUT, codeName: 'INVALID_INPUT' } and the field; plus valid read and search requests pass, and a limits override above the ceiling is refused.

Add the daemon-wide concurrency bound to repositorySource.ts. A small FIFO semaphore class SourceSlots(limit) with run<T>(timeoutMs, fn): Promise<T> waits at most timeoutMs for a slot, rejects with Error('budget exhausted waiting for a git slot') when the wait times out, and always releases in finally. A waiter whose wait timed out is removed from the queue (and its timer is cleared when it is granted), so a later release can never hand a slot to a dead waiter, which would leak the slot forever. Export one shared instance SOURCE_SLOTS = new SourceSlots(4) as the default, injectable through options.slots for tests. Add the wrappers readRepositorySource hands to openProjectGit: limitedRun(slots, run) and limitedHead(slots, head) acquire a slot within the timeout openProjectGit passes, then call the real runner with that timeout minus the time spent waiting. When nothing is left they refuse with the same budget message without calling the runner. Waiting for a slot can therefore never extend a request past its deadline.
Tests (repositorySource.test.ts): (1) with limit 2 and a deferred fake runner, 5 concurrent calls never have more than 2 in flight (record the maximum) and run in FIFO order; (2) a waiter that times out rejects with the budget message, and once the holders release the full limit is available again (two new calls start immediately), proving no leak; (3) a runner that throws still releases its slot; (4) the wrapper passes the reduced timeout to the runner, and refuses without calling it when the wait used the whole budget (vi.useFakeTimers or a controlled clock; restore real timers in afterEach, see mem gotcha-vitest-fake-timers-order-and-real-io). Error handling: every acquire path settles exactly once.

Add serveRepositorySource(state: StateManager, request: { taskId: string; commit: string; queries: SourceQuery[]; expectedPlanRevision?: number }, options?), returning RepositorySource & { taskId: string; planRevision: number }. This covers DoD 2: external analysis runs outside the fleet mutex, and the revision is revalidated before service.
1. If state.mutex.isHeld(), throw before any lock, process or task read: new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.NOT_ALLOWED, 'repository source analysis must run outside the state mutex; call it from a blocking: true path (see submit_plan)', { taskId }, 'SOURCE_ANALYSIS_UNDER_MUTEX'). McpAdapter runs every non-blocking tool handler inside the global reentrant mutex, so this guard makes 'outside the mutex' structural, not a convention.
2. Run validateSourceRequest. When expectedPlanRevision is present it must be a non-negative safe integer, else INVALID_INPUT 'expectedPlanRevision'.
3. Under state.runExclusive:
- task = state.getTask(taskId), else throw notFound('Task', taskId).
- Decode its revision with the same rule as taskStore's private decodeStoredPlanRevision: absent means 0 (legacy record); present but not a non-negative safe integer is INVALID_INPUT 'planRevision' (fail closed). Mirror the rule here. Do not import or edit src/state/taskStore.ts, which WORKING task F04 is changing (epic rail: serialize overlapping files).
- If expectedPlanRevision is given and differs, throw new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, ..., { taskId, expectedPlanRevision, currentPlanRevision }, 'SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH') with no process started.
4. Leave the lock and run readRepositorySource(state.projectPath, commit, queries, options).
5. Under state.runExclusive again:
- re-read the task; deleted means notFound;
- decode the revision the same way;
- if it differs from the captured one, throw new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, `plan revision changed from ${captured} to ${current} during source analysis; nothing was served`, { taskId, servedForRevision: captured, currentPlanRevision: current }, 'SOURCE_REVISION_CHANGED') and discard the analysis;
- otherwise return { taskId, planRevision: captured, ...result }.
Never write task state, attempts, activity or receipts: packet/receipt identity is F06/C01's. Do not edit StateManager.ts, whose 1500-line budget is enforced by stateModules.test.ts.
Tests: new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.service.test.ts using ToolTestHarness (src/tools/toolTestHarness.ts: init, setupMoeFolder, createTask, then state.load()). The fake run answers --show-toplevel with the test dir's realpath, config with '', rev-parse with the commit and ls-tree with one blob record. The fake head parks on a deferred.
(1) Called inside state.runExclusive, it rejects NOT_ALLOWED / SOURCE_ANALYSIS_UNDER_MUTEX and no runner is called.
(2) While head is parked, `await state.runExclusive(async () => 'free')` resolves. Race it against a 2 s timer so a regression fails instead of hanging.
(3) While parked, state.updateTask(taskId, { definitionOfDone: [...changed] }) advances planRevision; releasing head makes the serve reject STATE_CONFLICT / SOURCE_REVISION_CHANGED, and no content is returned.
(4) While parked, state.updateTask(taskId, { priority: 'LOW' }) leaves the revision unchanged, and the serve resolves with taskId, planRevision and the served item.
(5) The task deleted while parked gives NOT_FOUND.
(6) An expectedPlanRevision mismatch gives STATE_CONFLICT / SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH with zero runner calls.
(7) expectedPlanRevision -1, 1.5, '1' and null give INVALID_INPUT.
(8) A task created without planRevision serves with planRevision 0.
(9) Tasks created with planRevision 'x' and -1 give INVALID_INPUT naming planRevision, with zero runner calls.
(10) An unknown task gives NOT_FOUND with zero runner calls.
(11) The task JSON on disk is byte-identical after a successful serve.
Assert code and codeName on every refusal.

Checklist:

reopenReason:
QA round 2 on fcc0a4e. The gate is green: on a fresh whole-repo archive, `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 (161 files, 3960 passed / 15 skipped) and `tsc --noEmit` exits 0. All three round-1 fixes are pinned: removing each one fails its own named test.

REJECT: two repo-local-state escapes in the searchTree grep argv (repositorySource.ts:238). I missed both in round 1. Both reproduce end to end on the fcc0a4e provider with real git 2.43.
(A) Local `submodule.recurse=true` makes grep recurse into a populated submodule. An unscoped search then returns served and complete:true, with a match at sub/s.txt, which is content from inside a gitlink. Reads and scopes refuse that same gitlink as 'submodule'.

Evidence is in comment-a518c26a.

Keep the fix small (two flags plus two real-Git tests) and do not re-slice. comments.content:
QA round 2 (qa-b0c1741e) on fcc0a4e: REJECT. The provider has two new escapes that come from repo-local state. Both existed in round 1 and I missed them there.

Verified OK:
- fcc0a4e is on moe/work-2026-10-24, with parent 3bb12fc. Its source delta is exactly repositorySource.ts (+2/-2) and repositorySource.test.ts (+12/-2), plus the wrapper's board records. The snapshot's five task paths match the commit blobs.
- Test gate, on a fresh whole-repo `git archive fcc0a4e` (/tmp/qa-c02r2.ZO0AVV) with native Linux deps (lockfile equal) and env -i:
  - `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test`: exit 0. 161 files, 3960 passed / 15 skipped.
  - `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- The reopen fixes are pinned (harness /tmp/qa-c02r2-harness/mut.py). Dropping --no-column, the NUL-text guard or grep --literal-pathspecs each fails exactly its named test. Dropping both column guards fails 2 tests. Baseline passes 130/130.
- These local settings are already neutralised by the existing flags, so no action is needed: grep.patternType=perl, grep.extendedRegexp, color.ui and color.grep=always, core.ignoreCase, grep.lineNumber and grep.fullName=false, grep.threads, and sparse checkout.

Defect A, DoD 'Root/symlink escape is refused.':
- Cause: repo-local `submodule.recurse=true` makes `git grep <commit>` recurse into populated, active submodules. git-config documents that submodule.recurse applies to grep.
- Result: provider at fcc0a4e, real git 2.43, unscoped search 'hello' with gitlink `sub`. It returns status served and complete true, and the matches include {path:'sub/s.txt', line:1, text:'hello from SUBMODULE'}.
- Why it matters: reads and scopes at or under a gitlink are refused with 'submodule', but search serves exactly those bytes. The submodule's `.git` gitfile is a worktree file and can point outside the root.
- Fix: verified that `--no-recurse-submodules` stops the recursion even with the config set.

Defect B, DoD 'Partial/missing source remains explicit.':
- Cause: `-I` decides binary from attributes, which come from the working tree/index (even an untracked .gitattributes), .git/info/attributes, local core.attributesFile and diff.<driver>.binary.
- Result: provider at fcc0a4e with an untracked `.gitattributes` containing `a.ts -diff` (git status `?? .gitattributes`). A search scoped to the committed a.ts, which contains 'hello', returns status served, matches [] and complete true. That is a false negative caused by uncommitted bytes, which breaks 'committed-bytes-only'.
- Fix: with `-a`/`--text`, git never consults attributes, so a.ts matches. A binary blob's record then contains a NUL, so the existing guard makes it explicit truncated/undecodable-match.

Repros:
- /tmp/qa-c02r2-harness/{probe-sub.sh, probe-attrs2.sh, probe-config.sh}
- Provider end-to-end probe, in a scratch copy and not the shared tree: /tmp/qa-c02r2-e2e.hY99zc/repo/packages/moe-daemon/src/context/qaProbe.test.ts

Operator decision (REPL, 2026-10-25): re-slice C02 so it runs now, instead of blocking on C01 (packet contract, BLOCKED behind F03-F06) and R09 (snapshot transfer, BACKLOG). C02's dependsOn on C01/R09 was removed. C01 now depends on C02, so the packet adopts this provider's status/reason/limitation vocabulary instead of inventing a second one.
Rejected:

(c) Plain runGit maxBuffer: all-or-nothing, so a common caller search would return nothing.

(e) Exporting taskStore's decodeStoredPlanRevision: F04 is WORKING on taskStore.ts.
(f) Registering an MCP tool now: activation is out of scope, and an unregistered library needs no docs/MCP_SERVER.md section.
(g) Serena/semantic callers: C03's job.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- util/cachedPlanPaths.ts openProjectGit (from V01b) is the shared read-only trust envelope, also used by delivery/requiredChecks.ts. Extend it, never fork it.
- submit_plan is the blocking:true precedent: work outside the mutex, then revalidate under runExclusive.
- state.mutex is a public readonly AsyncMutex with isHeld().
- McpAdapter wraps every non-blocking handler in runExclusive (mem gotcha-daemon-global-mutex-dispatch).
- planRevision: absent means legacy 0. derivePlanRevision bumps it on a DoD, plan or executionContract change or PLAN_SUBMITTED; priority and comments changes do not bump it.
- ToolTestHarness writes .moe fixtures, and load() does not validate planRevision.
- submitPlan.test.ts cachedBranch() is the plumbing-fixture precedent.
- Verified on git 2.43:
  - the `grep -z -n` record format;
  - tree grep skips symlink and gitlink entries;
  - ls-tree prints a directory's children instead of the directory when another pathspec forces descent;
  - ls-tree on lnk/x alone prints nothing, so ancestors must be passed as pathspecs.
planningNotes.risks:
- A timed-out slot waiter leaking its slot.
- Deadline drift while waiting for a slot.
- A nondeterministic total cap.
- A missing scope reported as an empty search (false negative).
- The 32K Windows command line: covered by the pathspec budget.
- Large sibling directories along query paths can exceed the 1 MiB listing cap. The items then become explicitly unavailable; C04/C11 may revisit.
- Git paths are case-sensitive on case-insensitive filesystems, so a case mismatch reports missing (honest).
- Non-UTF-8 content.
- Fixture git inheriting a seat's GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE and writing to the PROJECT repository: strip every GIT_* variable.
- vi.mock hoisting: real-git tests go only in context/*.test.ts, never in cachedPlanPaths.test.ts.
- StateManager 1500-line budget: no edits there.
- MOE_* seat env and the Windows node_modules under WSL, for verification.
- Shared checkout: never revert, stash or commit peer bytes; the wrappers land.
- isEpicFinal is an order artifact; C11 owns the epic docs sweep and integration.

issues.description: Local repo config isn't masked. With `git config grep.column true` in the project, git 2.43 prints `<commit>:<path>\0<line>\0<col>\0<text>\n`. parseMatches folds the column into text, and the item comes back SERVED with text "1\u0000hello" (QA real-git probe). Fix: pass `--no-column` in the grep argv, and treat a NUL in decoded match text as undecodable-match. Add a real-git fixture test with grep.column=true.

Removing `--literal-pathspecs` from the grep argv survives all 189 focused tests. The 'does not interpret literal or pathspec metacharacters' case has no sibling the glob could match. Without the flag, real git also matches `literal1.ts` for scope `literal[1].ts`. Add a committed sibling `literal1.ts` containing `-hello` and assert exactly one match. The ls-tree mutant is equivalent (ls-tree doesn't glob), so no test is needed there.
